name: Consolidated Edison, Inc.
base_source: TTM adjusted (maintenance-proxy) OE: reported adjusted EPS FY2025 $5.70 - H1 2025 $2.91 + H1 2026 $3.00 = $5.79; cross-checked as TTM GAAP NI $2,217M - $134M after-tax MVP gain = $2,083M / ~360M shares. Engine base rejected: post-2022 capex is tagged PaymentsForConstructionInProcess, engine read capex=$0 for 2023-25; with real capex (~$5.25B/yr incl. removal) conservative OE is negative every year (FY25 -$445M, TTM ~-$1,300M). See analysis.md.
moat_justification: Legal monopoly delivery franchise in NYC metro with zero customer switching, multi-year rate plans and ~8.6-8.8% guided rate-base CAGR, 52 straight years of dividend increases — against a regulator that caps authorized ROE at ~9-10% (earned ~8.4%), rising NY political/affordability pressure (Chapter 58, 2026), long-run gas-network electrification/stranded-asset risk, and perpetual debt + equity issuance (shares 347M end-2024 to 370M mid-2026) diluting rate-base growth to mid-single-digit EPS growth.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 11.6x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
one_liner: Regulated NYC monopoly utility, moat 6/10 — but the engine's Tier B is a capex-tag artifact (real capex ~$5.25B/yr makes conservative OE negative); on TTM adjusted earnings of $5.79/share the $107.20 price (18.5x) yields only a 9.0% weighted IRR with IV@15% of $54.35 — it clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$54, or ~$43 with a margin of safety.
